note: Categories are scoped to one SE dimension. Each (dimension, code) pair belongs to exactly one category of that dimension.

categories.meaning: An AI agent produces review comments on pull requests, including the agent reviewing its own product's code and engineered AI reviewers (multi-agent, judge-filtered, ranked findings, custom-trained, tuned on developer feedback).
codes: ai code review on every pr
ai review findings aggregated and prioritised

categories.meaning: A person must approve before merge: mandatory peer review, human merge approval, code owners, readability approval, careful human review of critical code.

Rules for how people handle AI output in review: resolve the AI review before asking a colleague, author must understand and own AI-written code, disclose AI use; includes the review load this creates.
Written rules for reviewers: approval standard (code health), non-blocking nits, response-time targets, review rubric and style authority, review as mentoring.
Rules for what a submitted change looks like: small single-purpose PRs, motivation in the PR body, commit and title conventions, tests included, contributor agreement.
codes: structured commit and pr title convention

categories.meaning: Machine checks run before a human or AI reviews: pre-commit hooks, lint and type checks, agent evaluation on each PR, recurring review comments turned into lint rules.
codes: review findings turned into lint rules

categories.meaning: Review led by a security team or held after an incident, rather than routine PR review.
Evidence that changes are not reviewed through PRs: maintainers commit directly, no review policy.
Automated lint, build and test runs on each push or PR, including cross-platform matrices, presubmits, a single merge-blocking gate, split pre-/post-merge checks and agent evals in CI.
CI jobs or agent runs are isolated from secrets and the host: least-privilege workflow permissions, secret-free fork CI, sandboxed agent execution.

Investment in the machinery that builds code or runs agents at scale: build clusters and caches, queue-and-worker agent runners, cloud coding agents, local dev servers, redesigns of that infrastructure.
Releases are built and published by automation: tag- or PR-triggered publishing, continuous deployment, package-manager distribution.
Release or verification still needs a manual trigger, or no automated CI exists.
A stated release cadence of daily to every few weeks.
The team or company uses a build internally (including running the agent on its own operations) before external users get it.
Limiting who gets a change and undoing it fast: staged or invite-only rollout, feature flags, one-click or config rollback.
Version and compatibility rules, and publishing what each release contains: release notes, worklogs, generated or bilingual release docs.
Deterministic unit, integration, end-to-end, UI, performance and cross-platform tests, and how they are organised (test strategy, guidelines, framework migration, hermetic tests).
Techniques that make tests of LLM-based code repeatable: mocked model responses, retries and deflake runs, repeated eval runs with statistics.
Where and when tests run: on every PR, split pre-/post-merge, nightly, in parallel, in sandboxes or local dev servers, with eval cost limits; includes having no CI.
The agent runs the product's tests, clicks through the app, or hunts for bugs in its own codebase; the codebase is laid out so it can.
codes: agent finds and fixes its own bugs

categories.meaning: The agent or model is scored on eval suites: internal eval frameworks, public or third-party benchmarks, single/multi-turn and trajectory evals, simulated users, eval sets from real user data, eval metrics and eval-driven fixes.
codes: eval set from real user data
public model cards and research papers

categories.meaning: A model grades the agent's output or labels the eval data.
Quality is judged from real use before or after general release: internal dogfooding, A/B tests, early access or preview stages, SLO gates on a limited release, user and community reports.
Traces, step-level debugging, token and cost tracking of agent runs, and runtime self-checks.
Red-teaming, attack benchmarks, pen-tests and bug bounties, with failures fed back into training.
People confirm quality: bug bashes, manual test steps or screenshots in the PR, regression test required with a fix, author sign-off, a review board.
Bugs go through a public tracker with forms, templates, labels or a roadmap view.
Automation triages issues: AI duplicate detection, stale-issue closing, bot-driven assignment.
Confirmed bugs are routed to the team that owns the area, or tracked in an internal ticket system.
Reporters and community members supply reproduction logs, root-cause analysis or first-line support.
The agent hunts for bugs, plans or drafts fixes, and engineers review what it produced.
codes: agent finds and fixes its own bugs

categories.meaning: Security bugs come through bug bounty or disclosure programs and are patched quickly; attacks are turned into training data.
Production failures are traced, rolled back or recovered automatically.
Fixes, incidents and their redesigns are reported publicly: release notes, incident write-ups, engineering blog.
No SLA, labels or assignees; maintainers fix what they can, sometimes by direct commit.
Categories of bugs reported for the agent; kept so failure types can be compared across agents.
codes: bug pattern: agent loop and model handling
bug pattern: api and contract mismatch
bug pattern: input and data handling
bug pattern: resource and dependency leaks
bug pattern: version and platform regressions

categories.meaning: Engineers develop the product with AI agents: the agent writes most code, engineers plan with and manage agents, AI is mandatory in daily work, agent runs are monitored, repos ship agent config.
codes: agent writes its own product code

categories.meaning: What gets built is steered by the team's own use of the agent and by usage data.
Many quick prototypes or experiments instead of up-front specs; ship, learn, fix forward.
A develop-evaluate-refine loop where eval results decide the next change.
Each version follows a research milestone and ships with a paper or tech report.
codes: public model cards and research papers

categories.meaning: One repository and trunk, short branches, small changes gated by presubmits, large-scale automated changes, shared dev tooling.
Methodology defined by how releases flow: fixed cadence, internal-first, feature flags, semantic versioning and compatibility.
Two-to-four-person teams, one engineer title, ideas bottom-up, broad goals set from the top.
Named roles, sprints and recurring structured meetings with post-mortems.
Published principles for the agent's design, including security-first and human-in-the-loop design and redesigns that follow them.
Engineers ask the agent instead of colleagues, onboard with it, give feedback to an AI tool in-thread, or let it run team operations.
Communication defaults to open chat channels, documents and logs anyone can read.
Decisions travel in writing: mailing lists, design docs before work, decision records, written culture, a distributed team.
Spontaneous or scheduled face-to-face meetings, escalation to video, shadowing-based onboarding.
PR descriptions, commit conventions, code-owner requests and issue bot commands carry coordination.
codes: structured commit and pr title convention

categories.meaning: The team talks to the outside through blogs, tech reports, release notes, worklogs and outreach.
codes: public model cards and research papers

categories.meaning: Two-way channels with users and security researchers: forums, Discord, coordinated disclosure.
Context files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) and machine-readable docs aimed at coding agents.
Docs live in the repo and must be updated in the same or a paired PR, follow a standard, or are the tests themselves.
Docs or release notes are generated from code, migrations, commit titles or PRs, with human review.
codes: structured commit and pr title convention

categories.meaning: A hosted documentation site or per-version READMEs for users and builders.
Tech reports, papers and model cards document the model and agent design.
codes: public model cards and research papers

categories.meaning: Changes and internals are documented in release notes and blog posts.
Security model, policies and incidents are documented publicly.

not_practice.meaning: Definitions and product events coded for completeness; excluded from pattern counts.
